name: Sunshine Coast
tagline: Long surf beaches, rainforest hills and relaxed seaside towns an hour north of Brisbane
description: The Sunshine Coast stretches for nearly 70 km north of Brisbane, from Caloundra through Mooloolaba and Maroochydore to Coolum. Most of its draw is the white-sand beaches, many patrolled by surf life savers, with a salt-water pool at Kings Beach and kitesurfing at Golden Beach. Behind the beaches sit family attractions such as Australia's Big Pineapple, a wildlife zoo and a large aquarium. It is a holiday coast for Queenslanders as much as for visitors, so the pace is easy and the facilities are good.
whyVisit: Meet animals at zoos and aquariums
Explore lighthouses and headlands at Caloundra

goodToKnow.title: Swim between the flags
goodToKnow.detail: Swim only between the red and yellow flags on patrolled beaches, as lifeguard numbers vary by beach and season.

goodToKnow.title: A car is the easiest way
goodToKnow.detail: The coast is about 70 km long and the hinterland and attractions are spread out, so a car or tour makes it far simpler to cover.

goodToKnow.title: Busy school holidays
goodToKnow.detail: It is a popular Queensland holiday spot, so book accommodation early and expect crowded beaches in school holidays.

bestTimeBlurb: Winters are dry, sunny and mild, and the water is still swimmable. {months} also avoids the humid summer storms.

name: Noosa
tagline: Hastings Street, a sheltered surf beach and a coastal national park on the headland
description: Noosa is a resort area of low-rise buildings, upmarket shopping and dining, set along sheltered beaches, waterways and parks. Hastings Street fronts the main beach, and at its eastern end the Noosa National Park covers the headland. Noosaville sits quietly beside the Noosa River, and tours run up the river to the everglades. The name comes from the local Kabi Kabi word for 'shadow'.
whyVisit: Walk the Noosa National Park coast
Cruise the Noosa River to the Everglades

goodToKnow.title: Patrolled beach flags
goodToKnow.detail: Swim between the red and yellow flags; the beach conditions are posted on a blackboard near the surf club.

goodToKnow.title: Everglades tours run the river
goodToKnow.detail: River tours go the full length of the Noosa River to the Everglades, and most include a BBQ or tea stop at Harry's Hut.

goodToKnow.title: Pick your Noosa
goodToKnow.detail: The name covers several areas: Noosa Heads for Hastings Street, Noosaville by the river and Sunshine Beach to the south.

bestTimeBlurb: Mild, sunny days and calm seas suit the beach and park walks. {months} is the sweet spot.

name: Sunshine Coast Hinterland
tagline: Waterfalls, rainforest walks and farm-gate villages in the green hills behind the coast
description: The Blackall Range rises just inland from the Sunshine Coast, with hill villages such as Maleny and Montville and a string of small national parks. Kondalilla National Park has 327 hectares of subtropical rainforest, with Kondalilla Falls dropping 90 m, and Mapleton Falls drops 120 m. The 58 km Sunshine Coast Hinterland Great Walk starts near Lake Baroon at Montville and takes four to six days. Visitor centres, galleries and cafes in the villages make it an easy day trip from the beaches.
whyVisit: Walk to waterfalls in subtropical rainforest

goodToKnow.title: Book Great Walk campsites
goodToKnow.detail: Campsites on the Hinterland Great Walk have water, toilets and platforms, and must be booked with Queensland Parks.

goodToKnow.title: Busy in school holidays
goodToKnow.detail: Waterfall parks such as Mapleton Falls can be crowded in the holidays, so arrive early or visit midweek.

goodToKnow.title: Facilities at Kondalilla
goodToKnow.detail: Kondalilla has a car park, picnic areas, barbecues, toilets, a lookout and three walking trails.

bestTimeBlurb: Dry, cool days show the rainforest walks and lookouts at their best. {months} is the clearest.

name: Glass House Mountains
tagline: Volcanic peaks rising from a flat coastal plain, with walks and lookouts for every level
description: Captain Cook named these peaks in 1770, thinking they looked like glass houses as he sailed past. They are the cores of extinct volcanoes, formed 25 to 27 million years ago, rising from a flat plain north of Brisbane. Most of the range is protected as Glass House Mountains National Park, and the peaks hold rare heath and rainforest patches. Mount Beerwah, the highest at 555 m, has been closed to climbers since 2008 because of rockfall risk.
whyVisit: Climb Mount Ngungun for the view

goodToKnow.title: Beerwah is closed
goodToKnow.detail: The Mount Beerwah summit route has been closed since 2008 because of rockfall, so pick another peak to climb.

goodToKnow.title: No camping in the park
goodToKnow.detail: There is no camping inside the national park. The nearest options are Beerwah State Forest or motels in Beerwah and the township.

goodToKnow.title: Train to Beerwah
goodToKnow.detail: A train station in Beerwah offers frequent, usually hourly, services, so you can arrive without a car.

bestTimeBlurb: Cool, clear mornings suit the summit climbs. {months} avoids the summer heat and storms on the exposed rock.

name: Rockhampton
tagline: Queensland's beef capital on the Tropic of Capricorn, with caves, art and a riverside heart
description: Rockhampton, known as Rocky, is Central Queensland's regional centre and one of the state's oldest cities, founded in 1855. It sits almost exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn and is regarded as Australia's beef capital, so steakhouses are a local pastime. Visitors come for the Rockhampton Zoo and Botanic Gardens, the Heritage Village, the Dreamtime Cultural Centre and an extensive regional art gallery. Capricorn Caves lie 26 km north and Mount Archer gives views over the city.
whyVisit: Eat steak in the beef capital
See the view from Mount Archer

goodToKnow.title: Car makes it easy
goodToKnow.detail: Sights are spread out, and the caves are 26 km north on the Bruce Highway. A car or hire is simplest.

goodToKnow.title: Friday bridge traffic
goodToKnow.detail: Expect delays of about 10 minutes on Friday afternoons when crossing the bridges towards Yeppoon.

goodToKnow.title: Zoo feeding at 3pm
goodToKnow.detail: Feeding time at Rockhampton Zoo is 3pm. It sits next to the Botanic Gardens, so combine the two.

bestTimeBlurb: Dry, warm days suit the caves, zoo and lookouts. {months} avoids the heat and humidity of the long summer.
